place_fields.summary: Kali Tiger Reserve is a protected Western Ghats landscape comprising Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary and Anshi National Park, with tiger, leopard, elephant, gaur and hornbills recorded.

planning_attributes.description: Kali Tiger Reserve lies in Uttara Kannada and protects moist deciduous, semi-evergreen and evergreen forest; safari activities are offered from designated reporting points.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The reserve combines Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary and Anshi National Park as a contiguous protected landscape.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Visitor access is through designated forest tourism/safari arrangements; the Kali Tiger Reserve site identifies Phansoli as a safari reporting point.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Forest access is regulated; safari entry is through designated arrangements and reporting points.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Follow forest staff instructions and do not approach wildlife independently.

place_fields.vibe: black limestone monoliths in dense forest
place_fields.summary: Yana is known for the Bhairaveshwara Shikhara and Mohini Shikhara, dramatic black karst limestone formations surrounded by Western Ghats forest.

planning_attributes.description: Yana has two major rock outcrops, Bhairaveshwara Shikhara and Mohini Shikhara, with a Shiva cave temple below Bhairaveshwara; the area contains numerous karst formations.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: Bhairaveshwara Shikhara about 120 m; Mohini Shikhara about 90 m.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Local tradition links Yana with the Bhasmasura and Mohini story from Hindu mythology. GSI recognition in 2026 identifies the area as a geo-heritage site of national importance.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: From the nearest road head, the main rock outcrops are reached by a trek of about 0.5 km through forest.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Respect forest and temple rules and the protected geological setting.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The forest trail can be slippery; sturdy footwear is recommended, and the trail is not ideal for very young children or visitors needing assistance.
planning_attributes.notes: The Government of Karnataka district page places Yana about 31 km from Kumta and 40 km from Sirsi.

place_fields.vibe: cliffside sunset viewpoint with religious associations
place_fields.summary: Jatayu Teertha is a hilltop/cliffside spot in Dandebagh, Gokarna, overlooking the coast and associated locally with the Ramayana story of Jatayu.

planning_attributes.description: The site is a scenic cliffside viewpoint near Gokarna Main Beach and Kudle Beach, with panoramic sea views and a strong local religious/mythological association.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Local tradition identifies the spot with Jatayu, the Ramayana bird who tried to rescue Sita from Ravana and fell after the encounter.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Jatayu Teertha is in Hilltop, Dandebagh, Gokarna; visitors can approach from the Gokarna beach area by local road and walking/cliffside paths.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: No reliable authoritative source located for formal opening hours or entry fees; treat access as site-dependent.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Use caution near cliff edges and rocky descents. A 2025 drowning incident was reported while visitors watched the sunset near Jatayu Tirtha.
